script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 19. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

A child finds a rock with a fern printed inside—perfectly preserved from 300 million years ago.  That fern died before dinosaurs existed, before mammals, before most of what we know.  Yet here it is, a message across time.

Fossilization usually requires quick burial in sediment—keeping scavengers and bacteria away. Over thousands to millions of years, minerals dissolved in groundwater seep into bones and shells, gradually replacing organic material molecule by molecule. The shape persists; the substance transforms. Less than 0. 1% of all species that ever lived became fossils.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Everything leaves traces.  The way you live, the things you create, the relationships you build—they're fossils in formation.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Legacy Thinking - What Will You Leave.

Here's your activity: Imagine someone discovering 'fossils' of your life in 100 years. What would you want preserved? What traces are you currently creating—in writing, in relationships, in deeds? Create or strengthen one thing today that might last. This helps you consider the traces your life will leave behind.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about stories trapped in stone can be applied to legacy thinking - what will you leave. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
